decisions.title: Published on your public site under an unlisted, random path
decisions.detail: The page lives at /instacart-catalog-lab/m31hn8bvrzm4n1ohpu1c/ with noindex, nofollow, and the folder root shows a placeholder. It carries interviewer names and verbatim quotes because you asked for sources. Anyone with the URL can read it, and git history keeps every version even if we later remove the data. Same pattern as the private directory and baby planning pages.
decisions.question: Comfortable with named quotes at this path, or should I move the quotes behind initials until the interviewer-facing version?

decisions.title: Spent a small amount of your Anthropic API credit
decisions.detail: The photo reader ran Claude Sonnet and Claude Haiku on 91 products twice (the second pass measures run-to-run stability), about $7.20. Pre-labels ran Claude Haiku three times on each of 150 products; that cost was not logged and should be well under a dollar [VERIFY]. Nothing recurring is scheduled.

decisions.title: Automated lookups against the GFCO Product Finder
decisions.detail: GFCO has no API. Its robots.txt has no directives and its terms do not prohibit automated access, so the agent swept 238 brands, one request every 3 seconds, 523 requests in all, every response cached. Requests went out under an identified client. If GFCO objects later the cache is enough for the demo and nothing needs to be refetched.

decisions.title: Open Food Facts used through the documented API at published rates
decisions.detail: OFF's robots.txt disallows /api for crawlers, and their guidance is about 15 product reads a minute with the bulk export for anything larger. The agent used the documented API as an identified client within that limit and cached 609 products. Scaling past a few hundred products means downloading the bulk export, a multi-gigabyte file, so that waits for you.

decisions.title: Instacart look and the same left rail as the experience map
decisions.detail: Copied the IDS tokens and the rail pattern from the September experience map so the later interviewer-facing version needs a content pass and no redesign.

decisions.title: Gluten-free only, for now
decisions.detail: The lab scores one attribute deeply. The detector and scorer are written so other families (dairy-free, Big 9 allergens) slot in as new term lists and certifier sources.

decisions.title: No scraping of Instacart
decisions.detail: The lab uses Open Food Facts, USDA FoodData Central, the GFCO product finder, and the Kroger API (written, waiting on your credentials). Kroger is an Instacart retail partner, so the same finding lands on partner data without touching Instacart's site.

decisions.title: 402 products, chosen to surface conflicts
decisions.detail: Twelve gluten-free and twelve regular products in each of 13 categories, extra oats, and every genuine conflict the sweep found (76 of them outside the 13 categories). The sample is enriched on purpose, so its rates are not catalog rates. Every headline stat on the page carries its frame for that reason.

decisions.title: Verified means a GFCO match by UPC
decisions.detail: Other certifiers (GFCP, NSF, Beyond Celiac) are not checked yet, and a GFCO listing under a similar name but a different UPC carries no weight. Name matching would have certified regular Lee Kum Kee soy sauce, Barilla Elbows, and King Arthur all-purpose flour because their gluten-free versions sit next to them.

decisions.title: Implied wheat counts as gluten
decisions.detail: Bare 'flour', plain soy sauce, bread crumbs, and beer or ale count as gluten sources. Wheat-derived glucose syrup and dextrose get a small penalty only. The implied-wheat rule is the one most likely to produce a false conflict, which your gold labels will show.

decisions.title: Confidence weights are hand-set
decisions.detail: Fit them to your gold labels once those exist. Until then the slider measures against Claude Haiku pre-labels (3-vote majority, 145 of 150 unanimous).

decisions.title: Temperature 0 is not available on the 5.5 models
decisions.detail: Both agents hit the same API rejection. The reader measured stability with a second full run; the pre-labeler used a 3-vote majority. Worth knowing if anyone asks how you made model output repeatable.

decisions.title: The photo reader picked its own 91 products
decisions.detail: It ran in parallel with the pipeline, so only 40 of its products overlap the 402. Those 40 carry a label photo record in the evidence. A rerun of the reader on the pipeline's gold candidates would tie the two together.

decisions.title: Diagram A recommended for both subjects
decisions.detail: Four versions of each are on the page. A is the layered left-to-right layout with one arrow per stage. B through D are kept so you can compare.

decisions.title: Ad campaign and revenue projections held
decisions.detail: Not built in this pass. Pain points that touch acquisition or retention carry demonstration ideas, so the ads story has a place to land if you want it.

questions.title: Hand-check the headline conflicts before quoting any
questions.detail: Seven Sundays muesli (GFCO lists the UPC, three sources name barley and rye) and Kikkoman Less Sodium Teriyaki (GFCO lists the UPC, OFF and FDC name wheat) are the strongest, and either the registry row or the ingredient data is stale. Also check Canyon Bakehouse, Dave's Killer Bread, Cascadian Farm Fruitful O's, Nature's Bakery, Pepperidge Farm Mint Milano, and Dandy Blend.

questions.title: Keep or cut the label photo reader
questions.detail: It found 13 of 57 gluten-free listings contradicted by the package and costs about $1,200 per million products on Haiku. It also guesses at cropped claims and misreads small certification logos. My lean is keep, framed as a review-routing tool that can only hold or remove a claim, never add one.

questions.title: Ten [VERIFY] items in the Instacart current-state diagram
questions.detail: Kroger syndication path, Label Insight, stream versus batch split, ingest owner, Maple as pipeline runtime, partner ML models, Griffin feature store, whether a confidence score reaches downstream, allergen precedence, and attribute family owners. Most are better asked of Brittany or Tarang than asserted.

questions.title: About a dozen [VERIFY] precedents in the pain points
questions.detail: Real-world solution precedents that come from memory of public material. Check any you plan to say out loud. Several pain points also rest on soft confirmations, where the interviewer agreed with you rather than raising it.

questions.title: Kroger developer account
questions.detail: The Kroger client is written and skips cleanly without credentials. Creating the free developer app at developer.kroger.com is yours to do. Put KROGER_CLIENT_ID and KROGER_CLIENT_SECRET in jobbot3000/.env and rerun. Whether Kroger returns any dietary attribute at all is still [VERIFY].

questions.title: USDA FoodData Central key
questions.detail: The shared DEMO_KEY ran out after 320 of 402 products. All 150 gold candidates were covered first. A free data.gov key fixes the other 82; signing up is yours to do. Put it in .env as FDC_API_KEY and run python run_all.py.

questions.title: Who labels the gold set
questions.detail: You, in the labeling panel, 150 products, roughly an hour. Labels live in this browser only, so export them when done. A second labeler, such as the celiac friend you quoted in the jam, would let us report inter-rater agreement, the honest way to say how good a gold set is.
